title: Free City of Lübeck
capsule: The Free City of Lübeck was a sovereign city-state on the Baltic coast whose independence was confirmed by the reorganization accompanying the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire in 1806 and reaffirmed by the Congress of Vienna in 1815. As the medieval capital of the Hanseatic League, Lübeck retained its status as one of four German free cities (alongside Hamburg, Bremen, and Frankfurt) into the era of German unification. It joined the North German Confederation in 1866 and became a constituent state of the German Empire on 1 January 1871, retaining its senate government while losing formal sovereignty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. City boundaries are well documented through 19th-century German administrative records; Lübeck's modest urban territory was stable and precisely defined throughout this period.
